commit_scope: Three self-imposed blocks resolved at their causes: pulse respawned an http.bml listener every round because host_wait answers -2 where Linux refuses pidfd_open, so workers piled up at four cores; the API's runtime-event cache held one entry and was cleared on every request, so every reader refetched thousands of telemetry rows; and the runtime_events table kept 10.3 million request rows (7 GB) with no retention. Pulse respawns only on a real exit or a dead pid (host_alive); the event cache is per key and invalidated by endpoint family; telemetry past 30 days is trimmed at startup and every thousand writes.
evidence_refs: VPS on 2026-10-26 04:0x UTC: load 10 on a host with 60 % steal; coherence-network-pulse-1 at 437 % CPU, coherence-network-api-1 at 288 % with 344 zombie health-check curls and health probes timing out at 5 s; every Hostinger deploy since 2026-10-23 05:05 UTC failed because CI's 35-minute roll-forward watchdog cut the image build while the starved VPS compiled the kernel and built form-cli (run logs end inside kernel-builder step 5/5); the API ran the 23 October image, so #4139's ledger heal never reached production.

Pulse: form/runtime/fkwu-uni.c documents host_wait (list pid ms) as nothing() while the child runs, the exit status on exit, and -2 when the host cannot wait on a child's end (pidfd_open refused; Docker's default seccomp). pulse/main.bml treated any non-nothing answer as an exit and spawned a new listener each round while the old kept serving. The loop now respawns only when the wait answers a real status or host_alive(pid) says the pid is gone; `./fkwu --check ../pulse/main.bml` passes.

API: strace of the hottest thread (after a restart, with no request in flight) streamed runtime_events rows out of Postgres without end; pg_stat_user_tables showed 18,495 sequential scans reading 61 billion tuples; the table held 10,336,682 rows (7,092 MB), 8,252,070 older than 30 days, oldest 2026-06-18; its newest 200,000 rows are the web's polled routes (reactions/recent, concepts/voices/recent, presence/summary). runtime_service's events cache was a single entry keyed by one (limit, since, source, prefix) and cleared by every record_event, i.e. by every request.

Heals: runtime_service keeps up to 64 cached lists by key and a new event drops only the unfiltered lists and the lists of its own endpoint family; runtime_event_store.trim_older_than deletes past `runtime.events_retention_days` (30, file-backed config) in 50,000-row batches, run once per start in a daemon thread and once per thousand writes with a single batch; the operator trimmed production's 8.25 million old rows the same hour (see the rollout note). Pulse container stopped by hand first; the API restarted (health probes had timed out), answered ping in 5 ms, and the trace named the reader.

Proof: test_runtime_events_cache_is_per_key_and_invalidates_by_endpoint_family and test_runtime_event_store_trims_telemetry_past_retention; runtime, mesh and store test files 16 passed; the whole suite in the suite log of this push; the pulse check by the kernel. Rollout by hand on the VPS with nohup (outside CI's watchdog), then: pulse http.bml worker count stays 1 across rounds, API CPU idle, app.hati.earth 200, a malformed entry_key answers 422 (the #4139 heal live).
